summary: The timer callback ends with v2_playbook_on_stats, which prints the play duration with self._display.display and the format_string option; CALLBACK_VERSION and CALLBACK_NAME are required, CALLBACK_TYPE distinguishes stdout callbacks (only one can load), and since ansible-core 2.22 registered secrets are masked in results and Display() output, so callbacks writing elsewhere should call mask_secrets().
questions: Which callback attributes are required in Ansible 2.0 and later?
Why can only one stdout callback be loaded?
How do callback plugins mask secrets in ansible-core 2.22?

answer_card.title: Callback plugin essentials
answer_card.answer_md:
- `CALLBACK_VERSION` and `CALLBACK_NAME` are required for callbacks to work in Ansible 2.0 and later.
- `CALLBACK_TYPE` distinguishes `stdout` callbacks from the rest; only one stdout callback can be loaded.
- Print with `self._display.display(...)` rather than printing yourself.
- In ansible-core 2.22, task results and `Display()` output already have registered secrets masked. If your callback writes other data (task names, for example) to a file or external service, pass it through `mask_secrets()` first.
